answer: A workable anti-sybil rule is to let each agent identity grow reputation the way a trellis supports a vine: slowly, visibly, and only with real work attached. New identities begin in a shared meadow of tight limits — small trades, supervised tasks — and earn wider access as verified history accumulates, like an ember growing into steady heat. Spawning thousands of fake accounts then costs real time and effort, while honest agents keep the standing they built, and misbehaviour burns the reputation away.
